gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a roughly 60 kWh system actually costs. At US store prices on 2026-11-10, an EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X with 61.44 kWh (1 inverter + 10 Smart Extra Batteries) costs $27,289, or $0.44/Wh, with 12 kW of output. An Anker SOLIX E10 with 61.44 kWh (2 power modules + 10 B6000 batteries + Power Dock) costs $29,092, or $0.47/Wh, with 15.36 kW continuous. Neither system reaches 60 kW at its maximum size: 36 kW for the EcoFlow and 22.8 kW continuous for the Anker.
standout_why: I compared the cited us.ecoflow.com DELTA Pro Ultra pages, the ecoflow.com DPU X specs page, wattsandhours.com and solarwaypoint.com. The EcoFlow pages give prices for single units and bundles only. ChatGPT's own cards say 'Listed configuration, not full 60kWh system' and 'a 60kWh system costs more' without giving a number. wattsandhours gives no price and no 60 kWh setup. solarwaypoint (dated 2024-10-01) gives about $0.90/Wh, roughly twice today's $0.44/Wh, and tops out at 21.6 kW. No page lists the parts count, total price, weight or output for a 60 kWh build, and none says that no candidate can deliver 60 kW.
decides: For a 60 kWh reading of the question, the DELTA Pro Ultra X is the pick. It reaches 61.44 kWh on one inverter for $27,289 ($0.44/Wh), weighs about 1,189 lb and runs at 51.7 Wh/lb. The Anker SOLIX E10 needs two power modules plus a Power Dock to reach the same capacity: $29,092 ($0.47/Wh), about 1,421 lb, 43.2 Wh/lb. In exchange the E10 gives more output at that size (15.36 kW continuous against 12 kW). For a 60 kW output reading, neither consumer system qualifies. A 60 kW load would need 5 DPU X inverters (60 ÷ 12), and the system allows only 3. So the page should send 60 kW shoppers to commercial three-phase inverters such as the Sol-Ark 60K that ChatGPT showed.
